How many counties does Washington have, and who handles what?

Washington has 39 counties, and most of the paperwork behind a home sale runs through them. The county assessor values your property, the county treasurer collects the tax, and the county auditor records your deed.

The cities matter too. The state sorts its municipalities into four classes: first-class cities, second-class cities, code cities and towns. Wikipedia's municipal list counts 281 of them. Most are code cities. Even so, the city rarely touches your closing. The county does.

So the first step in any sale is knowing your county. A few of the busiest ones for our readers:

  • King County, home to Seattle, Bellevue, Kent and Renton. See the King County property tax guide.
  • Pierce County, home to Tacoma, Lakewood and Puyallup. See the Pierce County guide.
  • Spokane County, home to Spokane and Spokane Valley. See the Spokane County guide.
  • Clark County, home to Vancouver and Camas. See the Clark County guide.

Our county list further down links every city and county page we have written for the state.

How does property tax work if I am selling a Washington house?

Washington property tax is a county job from start to finish. The assessor values the home at 100 percent of its true and fair market value, and the treasurer bills and collects. The Department of Revenue oversees the system but does not collect the money.

If you disagree with your valuation, the appeal goes to the county board of equalization in the county where the home sits. Deadlines vary, so ask your assessor's office before you count on a date.

Tax dates matter when you sell with a bill outstanding:

  • The first half is due April 30 and is delinquent after that date.
  • The second half is due October 31 when the total is $50 or more.
  • Late tax on a home with four or fewer units carries 9 percent interest per year, computed monthly. Penalties of 3 percent and 8 percent apply to other property types, not to these homes.
  • After three years of delinquency the county treasurer can issue a certificate and foreclose the tax lien in the county's name, giving the owner 30 days after service to respond.

Unpaid tax is normally settled out of the sale proceeds at closing. For local detail, open the Washington property tax guide or the page for your city, such as Seattle, Spokane, Tacoma or Vancouver.

What does the real estate excise tax cost a Washington seller?

The seller usually pays it. Real estate excise tax, or REET, is due to the county treasurer where the property sits, on the date of sale, no matter when the deed is recorded. If the seller does not pay, the buyer becomes responsible and the tax can turn into a lien.

The state portion is graduated. The Department of Revenue lists these brackets for sales since January 1, 2023:

Part of the selling priceState rate
Up to $525,0001.10%
$525,000 to $1,525,0001.28%
$1,525,000 to $3,025,0002.75%
Above $3,025,0003.00%

Local REET is figured separately and added on top, so your total depends on the city or county. The department also lists higher bracket thresholds starting January 1, 2027. A $5 state technology fee applies to each transfer.

Some transfers are exempt, including inheritances, gifts and foreclosure related transfers, but only one exemption code can be claimed per transfer. Our Washington transfer tax page walks through the affidavit.

How does foreclosure work in Washington?

Most Washington foreclosures run outside court. A deed of trust may be foreclosed by trustee's sale, and the county auditor records that deed the way it would record a mortgage. A deed of trust on land used mainly for agriculture can instead be foreclosed as a mortgage.

The statute sets a fairly long runway for owners. These are the points that matter if you are behind on payments:

  • The notice of sale must be recorded and mailed at least 90 days before the sale, or 120 days when a pre-foreclosure letter is required.
  • The sale cannot happen less than 190 days after the date of default.
  • Sales take place on a Friday, or the next Monday when Friday is a holiday.
  • The model notice sets the reinstatement deadline at 11 days before the sale.
  • The trustee can postpone the sale, but for no more than 120 days in total.
  • The buyer at the sale gets possession on the 20th day afterward.

Selling before the auction date can end the process and stop the foreclosure. Talk to the trustee or a housing counselor about your exact dates, because each case turns on its own notice.

What should heirs know before selling an inherited house in Washington?

Start with who has authority. A personal representative who holds nonintervention powers may sell the decedent's real property without a court order. If no one has been appointed yet, the sale usually waits.

Washington also has a small estate affidavit. It requires that the probate estate, after liens and encumbrances and not counting a surviving spouse's community interest, stays at or under $100,000. At least 40 days must pass after death, and the claimant must notify other successors and wait 10 days. The statute text we reviewed addresses personal property and does not say whether the affidavit works for real estate, so ask a probate attorney before relying on it for a house.

A transfer on death deed is another route, because it passes the home to a named beneficiary at the owner's death. More detail sits on our probate page, the transfer on death deed page and the estate tax page.

Does the Washington homestead exemption affect a sale?

It protects equity from creditors, and it is mostly automatic. A home becomes a homestead once the owner occupies it as a principal residence. Land that is not yet occupied needs a declaration of homestead filed with the county recording officer.

The protected amount is the greater of $125,000 or the county median sale price of a single-family home in the preceding calendar year. That second number varies by county, which is why a King County owner and a rural owner may see very different figures. Homestead rules do not erase a tax lien or a deed of trust, so they rarely change who gets paid at closing. See the homestead exemption page for filing details.

Can I sell a Washington house that has tenants?

Yes, but the tenancy rules still bind the new owner and the timeline can be long. A landlord ending a tenancy for a sale of a single-family home must give at least 90 days of written notice under the version of the statute now in effect.

Points worth knowing:

  • The owner must make reasonable attempts to sell within 30 days after the tenant leaves, such as listing on the MLS.
  • If the home is not listed in that window, the law presumes the owner never intended to sell.
  • A fixed term tenancy cannot end early for this reason unless both sides agree in writing and the tenant has at least 60 days to move.
  • Nonpayment of rent, waste and nuisance follow shorter notice periods.

Many owners with occupied rentals choose a sale to a buyer who takes the house with the tenant in place. Our guides on landlord and tenant law and the eviction notice rules cover the notice types.

What does an as-is cash sale look like in Washington?

It means the buyer takes the house in its current condition and you skip repairs, showings and most of the wait. It does not remove the paperwork the state requires.

For a sale of improved residential property, the seller must deliver a disclosure statement within five business days after a written contract is accepted, unless the buyer waives it or the transfer is exempt. The buyer generally has three business days after delivery to rescind. The form is not a warranty of any kind.

An escrow agent typically holds the funds, pays off liens and has the deed recorded with the county auditor. Radon is one condition worth knowing about. The Department of Health encourages testing and notes the EPA action level of 4 picocuries per liter. Ask your county health office about local conditions.

Rules and dates change, so confirm each one with the county office that handles your parcel. See also our guides by city and county.

Frequently asked questions

How many counties are in Washington?

Washington has 39 counties. Property tax, deed recording and the REET all run through the county where the house sits.

Who pays the real estate excise tax when a Washington house sells?

The seller usually pays. It is due to the county treasurer on the date of sale, and the state portion starts at 1.10 percent on the first $525,000.

When are Washington property taxes due?

The first half is due April 30. The second half is due October 31 when the total tax is $50 or more.

Is Washington foreclosure judicial?

Usually not. A deed of trust can be foreclosed by trustee's sale, and the sale cannot happen less than 190 days after default.

Can I sell an inherited house before probate ends?

It depends on who has authority. A personal representative with nonintervention powers may sell without a court order, so ask a probate attorney first.

Does a seller have to give a disclosure statement?

In most sales of improved residential property, yes, within five business days of acceptance, unless the buyer waives it or the transfer is exempt.

How much notice does a tenant get when the owner sells?

For a single-family home, at least 90 days of written notice under the statute now in effect. Check with an attorney for your situation.

What is the homestead exemption in Washington?

It is the greater of $125,000 or the county median single-family sale price from the prior year, and it applies automatically to an occupied principal residence.
